course_name_original: FUNDAMENTALS OF ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING + INTRODUCTION TO ELECTRONICS
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering + Introduction to Electronics

learning_outcomes.text: Provide basic knowledge and methods for the analysis and synthesis of linear circuits in DC, AC and transient conditions, preparatory for later Electronics courses.
Acquire basic knowledge of electronic components and circuits.
Acquire basic knowledge of analysis techniques of first and second order linear systems in the frequency domain.
Acquire basic knowledge of transfer functions and harmonic response functions.
Acquire basic knowledge of the behavior and characteristics of feedback systems.
Acquire basic knowledge of techniques for evaluating the stability of linear systems.
Analyze the behavior of linear systems, with particular reference to first and second order systems, through analysis in the frequency domain.
Analyze the behavior and stability of feedback systems.

syllabus_topics: Analysis and synthesis on linear electric circuits in direct current
Analysis and synthesis on linear electric circuits in alternating current
Analysis and synthesis on linear electric circuits in transient operation
Mathematical models of linear electronic devices and systems
Analysis of linear systems in the frequency domain
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a single written test covering both "Industrial Electrical Applications" and "Elements of Electronics" modules. For the AIE part, students must demonstrate knowledge of circuit analysis and synthesis techniques in DC, AC, transient operation, and frequency analysis. For the Electronics Elements part, students must demonstrate knowledge and application of linear systems analysis and the ability to analyze simple circuits. The ability to solve exercises and answer simple theoretical questions is important.
